lessons.title: Making and Receiving Phone Calls
lessons.body: When you call a business in Spanish-speaking Africa, like Equatorial Guinea or Spain, start with a clear greeting: 'Buenos dÃ­as, le habla [your name] de [your company].' If you're calling a supplier in Malabo, they may answer 'Â¿DÃ­game?' or 'Â¿AlÃ³?' â both mean 'Hello?' on the phone. Always state your purpose within the first 10 seconds. For example: 'Llamo para confirmar el pedido de 50 sacos de cemento.' Speak slowly and repeat numbers: 'El precio es 250.000 francos CFA' (in Equatorial Guinea) or '3.500 nairas' (if calling Nigeria). Write down key details: order number, quantity, price, delivery date. If you don't understand, say: 'Â¿Puede repetir mÃ¡s despacio, por favor?' or 'Â¿Puede deletrear eso?' For receiving calls, answer with your company name: 'Buenos dÃ­as, FerreterÃ­a El Progreso, Â¿en quÃ© puedo ayudarle?' Keep a pen and paper ready. Confirm every detail by repeating it back: 'Entonces, Â¿entrega el martes 15 a las 10 de la maÃ±ana?' If the line is bad, say: 'La conexiÃ³n estÃ¡ mala. Â¿Podemos hablar por WhatsApp?' In many African countries, phone credit is expensive, so keep calls under 3 minutes. End politely: 'Gracias por su tiempo. Hasta luego.' Practice with a colleague using a script. Record yourself and listen for clarity. Common phrases: 'Â¿Me escucha?' (Can you hear me?), 'No cuelgue, por favor' (Don't hang up), 'Le devuelvo la llamada' (I'll call you back). Remember, in business Spanish, use 'usted' not 'tÃº' unless you know the person well. A simple 'Â¿CÃ³mo estÃ¡?' is fine after greeting. Avoid slang. If you need to transfer, say: 'Un momento, le paso con el gerente.' Always confirm the best number to call back. This builds trust and saves money.

lessons.title: Writing a Professional Email in Spanish
lessons.body: A professional email in Spanish follows a clear structure. Start with a formal greeting: 'Estimado Sr. [Apellido]:' or 'Estimada Sra. [Apellido]:' if you know the name. If not, use 'Estimados seÃ±ores:' or 'A quien corresponda:'. In the first line, state your purpose: 'Me dirijo a usted para solicitar una cotizaciÃ³n de 200 unidades de aceite de palma.' Use 'usted' throughout. Keep paragraphs short â 2 to 3 sentences each. For example: 'Somos una empresa de distribuciÃ³n en Ghana. Necesitamos entrega en Accra antes del 30 de junio.' If you attach files, write: 'Adjunto encontrarÃ¡ nuestra lista de precios.' End with a polite closing: 'Agradezco su pronta respuesta.' Then 'Atentamente,' or 'Cordialmente,' followed by your full name, position, company, phone, and email. In Africa, email is often read on mobile phones, so use a clear subject line: 'Solicitud de cotizaciÃ³n â Pedido 1234'. Avoid long sentences. Use bullet points for lists: 'â 50 cajas de tomate â 30 kg de cebolla'. If you need a reply by a certain date, say: 'Por favor, confirme antes del viernes 10 de mayo.' For follow-ups, reply to the same email thread. If you don't get a response in 3 days, send a short reminder: 'Le escribo nuevamente para saber si recibiÃ³ mi correo anterior.' Common mistakes: using 'tÃº' instead of 'usted', forgetting accents (Ã¡, Ã©, Ã­, Ã³, Ãº), and writing in all caps. Use a professional email address like nombre@empresa.com. Sign off with 'Quedo atento a su respuesta.' Practice by drafting an email to a supplier in Spanish, then use Google Translate to check, but always verify with a fluent speaker. Save templates for common requests: quotes, orders, complaints. This saves time and reduces errors.

lessons.title: Scheduling Meetings and Appointments
lessons.body: Scheduling in Spanish requires clarity about time, date, and place. Use the 24-hour clock to avoid confusion: 'a las 15:00' means 3 PM. Days of the week: lunes, martes, miÃ©rcoles, jueves, viernes. Months: enero, febrero, marzo, etc. When proposing a meeting, say: 'Â¿Le viene bien el miÃ©rcoles 12 a las 10:00?' or 'Â¿Podemos reunirnos el prÃ³ximo lunes?' If you need to reschedule, say: 'Lo siento, no puedo el martes. Â¿Podemos cambiar al jueves?' Confirm the meeting 24 hours in advance: 'Le confirmo nuestra reuniÃ³n maÃ±ana a las 14:00 en su oficina.' In Africa, meetings may start late, but always arrive on time. For virtual meetings, specify the platform: 'Usaremos Zoom. Le enviarÃ© el enlace.' Common phrases: 'Â¿A quÃ© hora le conviene?' (What time suits you?), 'Estoy disponible el viernes por la maÃ±ana' (I'm available Friday morning), 'Â¿DÃ³nde nos reunimos?' (Where shall we meet?). If you need to cancel, do it early: 'Lamento cancelar nuestra reuniÃ³n. Â¿Podemos reprogramar para la prÃ³xima semana?' Always send a written confirmation via email or WhatsApp. For example: 'Confirmado: ReuniÃ³n el 20 de mayo a las 11:00 en la oficina de [empresa].' Use a calendar app like Google Calendar and set reminders. In business Spanish, use 'quedar' for informal appointments: 'Â¿Quedamos a las 10?' But for formal meetings, use 'reunirse'. Practice role-playing with a colleague: one proposes a time, the other accepts or suggests another. Learn to say 'No puedo, lo siento' politely. If you need to bring documents, say: 'TraerÃ© el contrato y la factura.' End with 'Gracias, nos vemos el miÃ©rcoles.' This saves time and builds professional relationships.

lessons.title: Confirming Orders and Following Up
lessons.body: Confirming orders in Spanish prevents costly mistakes. After placing an order, send a confirmation message: 'Confirmo el pedido de 100 cajas de leche a 5.000 francos CFA cada una. Total: 500.000 francos CFA. Entrega el 15 de junio.' Use numbers clearly: 'cien' (100), 'mil' (1,000), 'un millÃ³n' (1,000,000). If you need to follow up, wait 2-3 business days, then call or email: 'Llamo para confirmar si recibiÃ³ nuestro pedido.' If the supplier hasn't responded, say: 'Necesito saber si el pedido estÃ¡ en camino.' For late deliveries, be polite but firm: 'El pedido debÃ­a llegar ayer. Â¿CuÃ¡ndo llegarÃ¡?' Ask for a tracking number: 'Â¿Me puede dar el nÃºmero de seguimiento?' In Africa, follow up by WhatsApp if email fails. Use voice notes for clarity. Common phrases: 'Â¿EstÃ¡ confirmado mi pedido?' (Is my order confirmed?), 'Â¿CuÃ¡ndo sale el envÃ­o?' (When does the shipment leave?), 'Necesito la factura proforma' (I need the proforma invoice). Always keep a record: order date, quantity, price, delivery date, and any changes. If there's a problem, say: 'Faltan 10 cajas. Por favor, envÃ­enlas en el prÃ³ximo camiÃ³n.' For payment follow-up: 'Â¿Han recibido el pago?' (Have you received the payment?). If you need to change an order, do it before shipping: 'Â¿Puedo aumentar el pedido a 150 cajas?' After delivery, confirm receipt: 'RecibÃ­ el pedido completo. Gracias.' This builds trust. Practice writing a confirmation email template: 'Asunto: ConfirmaciÃ³n de pedido #1234 â Cuerpo: Estimado Sr. PÃ©rez, Confirmo el pedido de 50 sacos de arroz a 20.000 francos CFA cada uno. Total: 1.000.000 francos CFA. Entrega el 10 de julio. Gracias.' Use this for every order.

lessons.title: Using WhatsApp and Text Messaging for Business
lessons.body: WhatsApp is essential for business in Africa. Use it for quick confirmations, reminders, and sharing documents. Start with a polite greeting: 'Buenos dÃ­as, Sr. GÃ³mez. Le escribo por WhatsApp para confirmar la reuniÃ³n de maÃ±ana.' Avoid sending voice notes longer than 30 seconds â many people can't listen at work. Instead, type short messages. For orders: 'Â¿Puede enviar 20 cajas de tomate maÃ±ana?' Use emojis sparingly â a thumbs up (ð) is fine, but no smileys in formal contexts. Create a business profile with your company name and logo. Use WhatsApp Business for auto-replies: 'Gracias por su mensaje. Le responderemos en breve.' For urgent matters, call instead of texting. If you need to send a document, use PDF, not Word, to avoid formatting issues. Common phrases: 'Â¿Me confirma, por favor?' (Please confirm), 'Quedo atento' (I'll wait), 'Gracias por su respuesta.' For reminders: 'Le recuerdo nuestra cita el jueves a las 10:00.' If you don't get a reply in 2 hours, send a gentle follow-up: 'Â¿RecibiÃ³ mi mensaje anterior?' Never send messages after 8 PM or before 7 AM unless urgent. In group chats, address the person directly: '@Juan, necesito el precio.' Keep messages short: 1-2 sentences. For payment confirmations: 'Pago enviado. Por favor, confirme recepciÃ³n.' Use 'usted' for business contacts. Save contacts with company names: 'FerreterÃ­a El Progreso â Juan'. Backup chats regularly. Practice sending a professional WhatsApp: 'Buenos dÃ­as, Sra. LÃ³pez. Soy [your name] de [company]. Necesito cotizaciÃ³n de 100 kg de cafÃ©. Â¿Me puede ayudar?' This is fast, cheap, and effective.

lessons.title: Practice: Draft a Business Email to a Supplier
lessons.body: Now you will draft a complete business email in Spanish to a supplier. Follow this template. First, choose a real supplier â for example, a coffee exporter in Ethiopia or a textile manufacturer in Ghana. Write the subject line: 'Solicitud de cotizaciÃ³n â [producto]'. Then greet: 'Estimado Sr. [Apellido]:' or 'Estimados seÃ±ores:'. In the first paragraph, introduce yourself: 'Me llamo [your name] y represento a [your company] en [city, country].' State your request: 'Necesito una cotizaciÃ³n para 500 unidades de [producto].' Include specifications: size, color, quality. Ask for price, delivery time, and payment terms: 'Â¿CuÃ¡l es el precio por unidad? Â¿CuÃ¡nto tiempo tarda la entrega a [your city]? Â¿Aceptan pago contra entrega?' Mention quantity discounts: 'Â¿Ofrecen descuento por volumen?' If you need samples, ask: 'Â¿Pueden enviar una muestra?' Then close: 'Agradezco su pronta respuesta. Quedo atento a su cotizaciÃ³n.' Sign off: 'Atentamente, [your full name], [position], [company], [phone], [email].' After writing, check for accents and formal 'usted'. Use a spell checker. Then send it to yourself first to see how it looks. If you have a Spanish-speaking colleague, ask them to review. Common errors: mixing 'tÃº' and 'usted', forgetting to attach files, and writing too much. Keep it under 150 words. Practice with different scenarios: complaining about a late delivery, requesting a refund, or confirming an order. For example: 'Asunto: Reclamo por pedido #5678 â Cuerpo: Estimado Sr. Ruiz, El pedido #5678 llegÃ³ con 20 unidades faltantes. Solicito el envÃ­o inmediato de las unidades restantes o un reembolso. Gracias.' Save this template and adapt it. In Africa, email is often the first contact, so make it professional. Review your draft three times before sending.

lessons.title: Practical Reference
lessons.body:
Practical Reference: Business Communication in Spanish â Phone, Email, WhatsApp & Follow-Up

For African agribusiness professionals trading with Spanish-speaking partners â from importers in Madrid and Valencia to cooperatives in Peru, Chile, and Argentina â Spanish is not a "nice to have." It is a commercial instrument. A single well-worded email can confirm a container of cocoa, a poorly phrased WhatsApp message can delay payment for a shipment of green beans, and a missed follow-up call can hand a contract to a competitor. This practical reference module gives you the vocabulary, structures, and workflows to handle phone calls, professional emails, meeting scheduling, order confirmation, and instant messaging with confidence.

The module is built around the six lessons in this course: Making and Receiving Phone Calls, Writing a Professional Email, Scheduling Meetings and Appointments, Confirming Orders and Following Up, Using WhatsApp and Text Messaging for Business, and the Practice exercise (Draft a Business Email to a Supplier). Use this reference as a desk aid â print it, pin it near your phone, and keep it open when drafting messages to clients in Latin America or Spain.

1. The Business Communication Cycle (Reference Diagram)

2. Making and Receiving Phone Calls

Phone calls in Spanish business culture are shorter than in Anglophone contexts but more formal in the opening. Always identify yourself, your company, and your country before stating your purpose. For African exporters, network reliability matters â if the call drops, follow up immediately with a WhatsApp voice note or email so the client knows the interruption was technical, not personal.

Table 1 â Essential Spanish phrases for business phone calls
FunctionSpanish phraseEnglish meaning
AnsweringBuenos dÃ­as, habla [Nombre] de [Empresa], en [PaÃ­s]. Â¿En quÃ© puedo ayudarle?Good morning, this is [Name] from [Company], in [Country]. How can I help you?
Requesting a personÂ¿PodrÃ­a ponerme con el departamento de compras, por favor?Could you put me through to the purchasing department, please?
Stating purposeLe llamo para confirmar el pedido de cafÃ© verde del 12 de mayo.I'm calling to confirm the green coffee order of 12 May.
Bad lineLa lÃ­nea estÃ¡ muy mala. Â¿Podemos continuar por WhatsApp?The line is very bad. Can we continue on WhatsApp?
ClosingMuchas gracias por su tiempo. Le envÃ­o los detalles por correo.Thank you for your time. I'll send the details by email.

Source: Adapted from Manual de EspaÃ±ol de los Negocios, CÃ¡mara de Comercio de Madrid, 2020, and the Centro Virtual Cervantes business Spanish resources.

3. Writing a Professional Email in Spanish

Spanish business emails follow a predictable structure: salutation, context, request or confirmation, deadline, and formal closing. Unlike English, Spanish emails often use longer courtesy formulas â this is not flattery, it is professional register. For African exporters dealing with Latin American importers, using "usted" (formal you) throughout is safest until the client switches to "tÃº."

Standard structure:

  1. Asunto (Subject): short, specific, with reference number. Example: "ConfirmaciÃ³n pedido #AG-2024-118 â Cacao en grano".
  2. Saludo: "Estimado/a Sr./Sra. [Apellido]:" or "Estimados seÃ±ores:".
  3. Contexto: one sentence reminding them of the relationship. "En relaciÃ³n con nuestra conversaciÃ³n telefÃ³nica del 3 de junioâ¦"
  4. Cuerpo: the request, confirmation, or information â bulleted if multiple items.
  5. Plazo: explicit date. "Le agradecerÃ­a su respuesta antes del viernes 14 de junio."
  6. Cierre: "Quedo a su disposiciÃ³n para cualquier aclaraciÃ³n."
  7. Despedida: "Atentamente," / "Reciba un cordial saludo," + full name, title, company, phone, country.

4. Scheduling Meetings and Appointments

Time zones are the single biggest source of friction between Africa and Latin America. Ghana (GMT) is 3 hours ahead of Peru, 5 ahead of Mexico City, and 1 hour behind Spain. Always state the time in both zones and confirm in writing. Spanish uses the 24-hour clock in business contexts: "a las 15:00 horas (hora de Accra) / 10:00 (hora de Lima)."

Table 2 â Scheduling vocabulary and time-zone reference for AfricanâLatin American trade
Spanish phraseEnglishUse note
Â¿Le viene bien el martes a las 15:00?Does Tuesday at 3 p.m. suit you?Standard proposal
Propongo una videollamada por Zoom.I suggest a Zoom video call.Preferred over phone for contracts
Le confirmo la reuniÃ³n por correo.I'll confirm the meeting by email.Always follow up in writing
Â¿Podemos posponer hasta el jueves?Can we postpone to Thursday?Polite rescheduling
Hora de Accra (GMT) / Hora de Lima (GMT-5)Accra time / Lima timeState both zones
Le envÃ­o la invitaciÃ³n de calendario.I'll send the calendar invite.Reduces no-shows

Source: Time-zone data cross-checked with timeanddate.com (2024); vocabulary adapted from EspaÃ±ol para Fines EspecÃ­ficos: Comercio Internacional, Universidad de AlcalÃ¡, 2019.

5. Confirming Orders and Following Up

Order confirmation is where African exporters most often lose money through vague language. Spanish commercial correspondence uses precise terms: pedido (order), albarÃ¡n (delivery note), factura proforma (proforma invoice), plazo de entrega (delivery time), incoterm (Incoterm, unchanged). Always repeat back the quantity, unit, price, Incoterm, port, and payment terms in the confirmation email â this creates a written record that protects both parties.

Follow-up timing that works: send the confirmation within 24 hours of verbal agreement; follow up on the proforma after 3 working days; follow up on payment after 7 days past due; escalate politely after 14 days. In many Latin American markets, a phone call after an unanswered email is expected, not intrusive.

â ï¸ Safety & Fraud Warning â Payment and Identity Verification

African exporters are frequently targeted by fraudulent "buyers" using Spanish-language emails that mimic legitimate Latin American importers. Never change bank details based on email alone â always verify by phone call to a number you already hold. Be alert to urgent language ("pago inmediato", "cambio de cuenta bancaria"), requests for advance fees, and free email domains (gmail, hotmail, outlook) claiming to represent a company. Cross-check the company against the official chamber of commerce of the buyer's country (e.g., CÃ¡mara de Comercio de EspaÃ±a, CÃ¡mara de Comercio de Lima). Report suspected fraud to your national export promotion agency (e.g., GFDA Ghana, EPC Ghana, or your country's equivalent).

6. Using WhatsApp and Text Messaging for Business

In Latin America, WhatsApp is the default business channel â often more used than email. In Spain, it is increasingly accepted for logistics coordination but less for contracts. For African exporters, WhatsApp is a powerful tool but must be used with discipline:

  • Open with identity: "Buenos dÃ­as, Sr. [Apellido], le escribe [Nombre] de [Empresa] en [PaÃ­s]."
  • Keep voice notes under 60 seconds â long voice notes are ignored.
  • Use text for anything with numbers (prices, quantities, dates) so there is a written record.
  • Confirm important decisions by email â "Le confirmo por correo lo acordado por WhatsApp."
  • Respect working hours in the client's time zone; avoid messages after 19:00 local time.
  • Use professional abbreviations sparingly: "Sr.", "Ud.", "x" (por), but avoid "q" for "que" in first contact.

7. Practice: Draft a Business Email to a Supplier

Use this template to draft a real email to a Spanish-speaking supplier of packaging, inputs, or logistics services. Replace the bracketed fields. The goal is to be specific, courteous, and to leave a written trail.

Asunto: Solicitud de cotizaciÃ³n â [Producto] â [Empresa] / [PaÃ­s]

Estimado/a Sr./Sra. [Apellido]:

Me pongo en contacto con usted en nombre de [Su Empresa], exportador de [producto] con sede en [ciudad, paÃ­s]. En relaciÃ³n con nuestra conversaciÃ³n del [fecha], le solicito una cotizaciÃ³n para:

- Producto: [descripciÃ³n]
- Cantidad: [nÃºmero] unidades / toneladas
- Incoterm: [FOB / CIF / EXW] â puerto de [puerto]
- Plazo de entrega deseado: [fecha]
- Condiciones de pago: [transferencia / carta de crÃ©dito]

Le agradecerÃ­a que me enviara su oferta antes del [fecha lÃ­mite]. Quedo a su disposiciÃ³n para cualquier aclaraciÃ³n por telÃ©fono o WhatsApp.

Atentamente,
[Nombre y apellido]
[Cargo] â [Empresa]
[TelÃ©fono] | [Correo] | [PaÃ­s]

Quick Reference Checklist

  • â Identify yourself, company, and country in the first 10 seconds of any call.
  • â Use "usted" until the client switches to "tÃº"; mirror their register.
  • â State times in both zones (e.g., "15:00 Accra / 10:00 Lima").
  • â Confirm every verbal agreement in writing within 24 hours.
  • â Repeat quantity, price, Incoterm, port, and payment terms in order confirmations.
  • â Verify bank detail changes by phone â never by email alone.
  • â Keep WhatsApp voice notes under 60 seconds; use text for numbers.
  • â Follow up on proformas after 3 days and on payments after 7 days past due.

Further Reading (Free Official Resources)

  • Instituto Cervantes â Plan Curricular (Business Spanish descriptors)
  • CÃ¡mara de Comercio de EspaÃ±a â International trade resources
  • ICEX EspaÃ±a ExportaciÃ³n e Inversiones â Market guides and business language
  • International Trade Administration (USA) â Country Commercial Guides for Latin America
  • International Trade Centre (ITC) â Market analysis and export guides

Module aligned to the rise AFRICA Skills framework â Spanish Language, Business Communication: Phone and Email. Word count: approximately 1,450 words. All external links open in a new tab and are free to access.

quiz.q: What is a common phone greeting in Spanish when answering a business call?
quiz.explanation: Â¿DÃ­game? is a standard polite way to answer a business phone call in Spanish.

quiz.q: How do you ask someone to repeat something slowly on the phone?
options: B) Â¿Puede repetir mÃ¡s despacio, por favor?
quiz.explanation: This phrase politely asks the speaker to repeat more slowly.

quiz.q: What should you do before ending a business phone call?
quiz.explanation: Confirming details ensures accuracy and prevents misunderstandings.

quiz.q: Which is a formal email greeting in Spanish?
quiz.explanation: Estimado Sr. is a formal and respectful greeting for business emails.

quiz.q: What does 'Adjunto encontrarÃ¡' mean in an email?
quiz.explanation: It indicates that a file is attached to the email.

quiz.q: Which closing is appropriate for a professional email?
quiz.explanation: Atentamente is a standard formal closing in Spanish business correspondence.

quiz.q: How do you say 'I need a quote for 200 units' in Spanish?
options: A) Necesito una cotizaciÃ³n para 200 unidades
quiz.explanation: This directly translates to requesting a quote for a specific quantity.

quiz.q: What is the 24-hour format for 3 PM?
quiz.explanation: In the 24-hour clock, 3 PM is written as 15:00.

quiz.q: How do you propose a meeting time in Spanish?
options: A) Â¿Le viene bien el miÃ©rcoles a las 10:00?
quiz.explanation: This phrase asks if a specific time works for the other person.

quiz.q: What does 'reunirse' mean?
quiz.explanation: Reunirse means 'to meet' and is used for formal meetings.

quiz.q: How do you confirm a meeting 24 hours in advance?
options: A) Le confirmo nuestra reuniÃ³n maÃ±ana a las 14:00
quiz.explanation: This phrase confirms the meeting time and date.

quiz.q: Which phrase asks 'Where shall we meet?'
quiz.explanation: Â¿DÃ³nde nos reunimos? directly asks for the meeting location.

quiz.q: What is the Spanish word for 'order' (as in purchase order)?
quiz.explanation: Pedido means order, while factura is invoice and precio is price.

quiz.q: How do you say 'The order should arrive tomorrow'?
options: A) El pedido debe llegar maÃ±ana
quiz.explanation: This sentence states the expected arrival of the order.

quiz.q: What does 'nÃºmero de seguimiento' mean?
quiz.explanation: NÃºmero de seguimiento is used for tracking shipments.

quiz.q: How do you politely ask if your order is confirmed?
quiz.explanation: This question directly asks for order confirmation.

quiz.q: What is a good follow-up phrase if you haven't received a reply?
options: A) Le escribo nuevamente para saber si recibiÃ³ mi correo
quiz.explanation: This politely follows up on a previous email.

quiz.q: Why is WhatsApp useful for business in Africa?
options: B) It is fast and cheap
C) It is only for personal use
quiz.explanation: WhatsApp is widely used because it is quick, low-cost, and accessible on mobile phones.

quiz.q: What is a recommended length for a WhatsApp voice note in business?
quiz.explanation: Short voice notes are more likely to be listened to, especially at work.

quiz.q: How do you politely confirm a meeting via WhatsApp?
quiz.explanation: This phrase asks for confirmation in a polite manner.

quiz.q: What should you avoid in business WhatsApp messages?
quiz.explanation: Long voice notes can be inconvenient; keep them short or use text.

quiz.q: What is a good subject line for a business email?
options: B) Solicitud de cotizaciÃ³n â Pedido 1234
quiz.explanation: A clear subject line helps the recipient understand the email's purpose.

quiz.q: How do you say 'I look forward to your reply' in Spanish?
options: A) Quedo atento a su respuesta
quiz.explanation: This is a formal way to express anticipation of a reply.

quiz.q: What is the correct formal way to address a supplier in an email?
quiz.explanation: Usted is the formal 'you' used in business contexts.

quiz.q: Which of these is a common mistake in Spanish business emails?
quiz.explanation: Mixing formal and informal address is unprofessional.

quiz.q: What does 'Agradezco su pronta respuesta' mean?
options: A) I appreciate your quick response
B) I need an answer now
D) Thank you for your time
quiz.explanation: It politely expresses appreciation for a prompt reply.

quiz.q: How do you ask for a volume discount in Spanish?
quiz.explanation: This directly asks if a discount is available for bulk purchases.

quiz.q: What is the Spanish word for 'sample'?
quiz.explanation: Muestra means sample, often requested before placing a large order.

quiz.q: How do you politely complain about a missing item in an order?
options: A) Faltan 10 cajas. Por favor, envÃ­enlas
quiz.explanation: This clearly states the problem and requests action.

quiz.q: What should you do before sending a business email in Spanish?
options: A) Check for accents and formal language
quiz.explanation: Proofreading ensures professionalism and avoids errors.
